newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power supported by cold forecast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power supported by cold forecast.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were mostly higher Wednesday, as traders awaited the arrival of much cooler temperatures on Thursday.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be about five to 12 degrees F below-normal Thursday, dropping to 10-20 degrees below-normal this weekend, the National Weather Service reported.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Thursday were at least another $1 higher in the $22.00-23.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, with some deals reported done at $24.00.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in northern TVA for Thursday were assessed around $15.00, traders said.

At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Thursday delivery were in convergence with the TVA market in the $22.50-23.50 range as most buyers purchased power on an hourly basis.

"Everyone's going to be conservative. They're holding onto what they have," one market source said, noting the changing weather patterns are creating a larger hourly market, where offers were heard as high as $35.00 per MWh.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was notionally around $13.00.
"They're now saying temperatures might get down into the high-30s tomorrow. Yesterday they were saying high-40s," one trader said, referring to the revised Florida forecast.
Hourly prices for firm, peak power in Florida were talked in the $20.00-23.00 range.
Separately, South Carolina-owned Santee Cooper said its 270 megawatt coal unit will likely be back on-line at 2000 EST Wednesday after tripping off line earlier today.
Helping to support the market were sustained high natural gas prices. Along the Gulf Coast, prices soared again near $4 per million British thermal units but then settled into the $3.70s and $3.60s.
